activities.title: Free Basic Education & ICT Edutainment for Children (Ages 5–12)
activities.summary: Regular free training workshops teaching children computer literacy, hardware components disassembly, typing, and introductory science.
activities.description:
### Empowering the Next Generation Through Hands-On Science and ICT

At the Bindir Knowledge Development Centre International (BKC), we believe quality basic education is a fundamental right. One of our core daily activities provides **completely free training to children aged 5 to 12 years old**.

During these regular interactive sessions, young pupils from surrounding public schools and under-served communities gather in our air-conditioned computer hall to get hands-on experience with personal computers, educational software, and basic science kits.

#### Key Objectives:
* Demystify computers and digital technology at an early age.
* Provide hands-on hardware exposure (disassembling and understanding CPU parts, motherboards, and power supplies).
* Spark foundational curiosity in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics).
* Foster peer collaboration across private and public school pupils.
activities.location: BKC Training Lab, No 12 Mallum Hamid Street, Yola Town, Adamawa State
activities.impact: Over 1,200 children have completed introductory computer literacy modules with zero fees charged to families.
activities.partnersInvolved: Adamawa State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Community Youth Volunteers

activities.title: 2025 International Day of the Girl Child: Empowering Out-of-School Girls
activities.summary: Special outreach program providing foundational literacy, numeracy, school supplies, and structured enrollment pathways for out-of-school girls in Adamawa.
activities.description:
### Bringing Hope and Schooling to Out-of-School Young Girls

To commemorate the International Day of the Girl Child, BKC spearheaded a high-impact community outreach project dedicated strictly to **out-of-school girl-children** across Yola South and surrounding rural communities.

Northern Nigeria continues to face significant challenges with out-of-school children, with girls disproportionately affected. BKC leveraged its community trust to mobilize parents, community leaders, and local teachers to identify vulnerable girls, organize basic literacy and numeracy classes, and distribute school uniforms, bags, and notebooks.

#### Highlights:
* Comprehensive data collection and profiling of out-of-school girls.
* Counseling and community dialogues with parents on the lifelong value of girl-child education.
* Re-enrollment partnerships with public primary schools in Yola South.
* Ongoing mentorship and revision support hosted at BKC facilities.
activities.impact: 650 out-of-school girls profiled and provided with educational supplies, with over 320 successfully re-enrolled into formal primary schools.
activities.partnersInvolved: Adamawa Women Affairs, Local Community Leaders, Volunteer Mentors

activities.title: National Conference for Primary School Headmasters (Adamawa State Pilot)
activities.summary: Convening headmasters from all 21 Local Government Areas of Adamawa State to raise teacher morale, introduce modern ICT curricula, and build professional networks.
activities.description:
### Elevating the Morale and Professional Standing of Primary School Leaders

Primary school headmasters are the foundational pillars of national education, yet their status, tools, and professional networks are often overlooked. BKC has pioneered a groundbreaking initiative: the **National Conference for Primary School Headmasters**.

Implemented state-by-state, the initiative commenced with a pilot across all 21 Local Government Areas of Adamawa State, covering both public and private primary institutions.

#### Conference Features:
* Formal accreditation and customized conference kit (Conference bag, official name tag, jotter, executive pen, and souvenir).
* Expert resource persons presenting papers on modern teaching pedagogies, digital learning tools, and school administration.
* Official Certificates of Attendance awarded to every participating headmaster.
* Fellowship sports tournament (Table Tennis and Badminton Novelty Matches) hosted in honour of the headmasters.
* Establishment of ongoing peer networks between private and public school leaders.
activities.location: BKC Grand Conference Hall, Yola Town
activities.impact: 850 Headmasters and senior primary school administrators trained across all 21 Adamawa LGAs, preparing the model for national rollout across 774 LGAs in Nigeria.
activities.partnersInvolved: Federal Ministry of Education, National Teachers Institute (NTI), Adamawa State Government

activities.title: Community High-Speed V-SAT Internet & Free Student Revision Hub
activities.summary: Providing round-the-clock free quiet study space, high-speed V-SAT internet connectivity, and educational audiovisual facilities for community students.
activities.description:
### Bridging the Digital Divide with High-Speed Community Internet

In many parts of northern Nigeria, unstable power grids and high mobile data costs prevent students from accessing online academic repositories, research papers, and examination preparation materials.

BKC invested in a dedicated **V-SAT satellite internet installation** combined with backup power and modern reading spaces. We open our doors daily to students, pupils, and researchers needing a safe, quiet, and digitally connected environment to study for WAEC, NECO, JAMB, and university assessments.

#### Facilities Provided:
* Dedicated V-SAT bandwidth with uninterrupted WiFi covering the entire complex.
* 60+ computer terminals equipped with educational software.
* Quiet study cubicles and group discussion breakout rooms.
* Free printing and scanning for academic revision notes.
activities.location: BKC Center, Makama "B" Ward, Yola Town
activities.impact: Over 3,400 secondary and tertiary students have utilized the facility for exam revision and academic research.
activities.partnersInvolved: Patron HRH The Lamido of Adamawa, Yola South Community Association

activities.title: Youth Science Edutainment & Vocational Technology Mentorship
activities.summary: Hands-on electronics, robotics kits, and career orientation for secondary school leavers and aspiring young innovators.
activities.description:
### Inspiring Technological Innovation and Entrepreneurial Skills

To drive sustainable community development, BKC established a dedicated **Assorted Technology Kits & Science Edutainment Lab** alongside our 2 business incubator suites.

Under the leadership of Founder Engr. Umar B. Bindir PhD FNA (renowned engineer and former Director-General of NOTAP), our mentors guide adolescent youth through real-world science applications, basic electrical circuitry, renewable solar technology, and career opportunities in engineering and agriculture.

#### Program Pillars:
* Practical science experiments replacing theoretical rote learning.
* Introduction to entrepreneurship and commercializing local innovations.
* Career counseling matching youth talents with tertiary degree programs and vocational certifications.
activities.location: BKC Innovation Lab & Technical Services Suites, Yola
activities.impact: 820 youth mentored, with 45 youth successfully admitted into university engineering and computer science programs.
activities.partnersInvolved: Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE), NOTAP Technology Innovation Network
